//: Fully-qualified C++ names (classes, methods, ctors, functions) to always skip, for cases the scanner can't detect heuristically (e.g. a method that's technically bindable but semantically unsafe to expose as-is). Extend as needed.
//_broken_headers: These are all structurally wrappable, but their declaring header (or one it drags in, e.g. generic/allocators/dynamic_aligned_allocator.h) fails to compile under GCC's -Wtemplate-body (missing #include <vector>/<cassert>, undeclared aligned_free/S_ERROR in template bodies) -- a pre-existing bug in Simulant itself, unrelated to the generated bindings. Remove these once that's fixed upstream.
//_unimplemented: Declared in a header but with no matching definition anywhere in Simulant -- either never implemented at all, or (circle/circle_outline) the .cpp defines a different, undeclared overload instead (an apparent stale header left over from a signature change). Either way a pre-existing engine bug, not a generator issue -- wrapping the declared signature mechanically produces a linker error the moment anything else in the same source file (e.g. Texture::width(), or any other function in functions.cpp) is used, since static libraries link at object-file granularity. Remove once fixed upstream.
//_platform_conditional: Declared behind an #ifdef the *scanning* platform happens to satisfy (this is always run on a real desktop OS) but that a cross-compiled target might not -- cgen.py has no per-platform notion of what it's generating for, so a method visible when scanning is assumed to exist everywhere the resulting bindings get compiled. Confirmed cross-compiling for PSP: SceneManager::register_scene_from_library is `#ifdef __linux__`-gated (dlopen-based dynamic scene loading, meaningless without a dynamic loader), so PSP's build of the real engine simply doesn't have it, and the mechanically generated wrapper calling it fails with 'no member named ...'. This does mean desktop C/Vala consumers lose access to this one function too -- an acceptable trade-off for now over teaching the generator about per-platform conditional compilation; revisit if that's ever needed for more than this one case.
